## Purpose

This report presents the reproducible figure set created by
`scripts/visualize-maize-data.R`. The graphics examine distributions, temporal
patterns, and paired observations and prepare questions for later descriptive
analysis. They do not establish stationarity or causal effects.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(readr)

registry_file <- here("metadata", "artifacts.csv")
if (!file.exists(registry_file)) {
  stop("Run Rscript scripts/visualize-maize-data.R before rendering.")
}

registry <- read_csv(registry_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
figure_state <- registry |>
  filter(
    artifact %in% c(
      "figures/maize-yield-distribution.png",
      "figures/maize-yield-trends.png",
      "figures/growing-season-precipitation-trends.png",
      "figures/yield-versus-precipitation.png",
      "figures/maize-yield-communication.png"
    )
  )
```

## Figure artifact state

The project-wide artifact registry records the current SHA-256 checksum and the
most recent detected change for each generated figure. A checksum identifies
the exact file; it does not assess visual quality or interpretation.

```{r}
#| label: figure-artifact-state
figure_state |>
  select(
    artifact,
    current_sha256,
    last_changed_at,
    last_change_detected_by
  ) |>
  kable()
```

## Maize-yield distribution

```{r}
#| label: fig-yield-distribution
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of annual maize-yield observations."
#| fig-alt: "Histogram of maize yield in tonnes per hectare for country-year observations from nine selected countries between 1990 and 2022."
include_graphics(here("figures", "maize-yield-distribution.png"))
```

The visible shape combines observations from countries with different yield
levels and trajectories. It depends on the documented 0.25 t/ha bin width and
should not be interpreted as one homogeneous population distribution.

## Maize-yield trends

```{r}
#| label: fig-yield-trends
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Maize-yield observations over time using common-scale country panels."
#| fig-alt: "Nine faceted line charts showing annual maize yield from 1990 to 2022, with one panel for each selected country and a shared vertical scale."
include_graphics(here("figures", "maize-yield-trends.png"))
```

Common vertical scales support comparison of absolute yield levels. The lines
connect ordered annual observations within each country; they do not imply
measurements between years or explain why trajectories differ. Persistent
changes in level, such as the increase visible for South Africa, motivate a
closer assessment of whether the mean is stable over time.

## Growing-season precipitation over time

```{r}
#| label: fig-precipitation-trends
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Growing-season precipitation estimates over time using common-scale country panels."
#| fig-alt: "Nine faceted line charts showing annual October-April growing-season precipitation from 1990 to 2022, with one panel for each selected country and a shared vertical scale."
include_graphics(
  here("figures", "growing-season-precipitation-trends.png")
)
```

CHIRPS values are seasonal totals of country-area mean daily estimates. They
do not measure exposure specifically over maize-growing land and conceal
within-country rainfall variation. Using the same period and panel structure
as the yield plot makes it possible to compare temporal patterns without
combining variables with different units on a dual-axis graphic.

## Visual questions about temporal stability

Read the two time-series figures together. Ask whether each country series
appears to have a stable level and variability, whether adjacent observations
are similar, and whether unusual years or persistent changes are visible.
Yield and precipitation need not have the same temporal structure even though
both are observed at the country-year grain.

These plots can reveal reasons to question a stationarity assumption, but they
cannot prove stationarity or distinguish a deterministic trend from a unit
root. The descriptive-analysis stage quantifies period changes and temporal
dependence before modeling decisions are made.

## Yield and precipitation

```{r}
#| label: fig-yield-precipitation
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Maize yield and growing-season precipitation by country."
#| fig-alt: "Nine faceted scatterplots of maize yield against growing-season precipitation, where each point represents one country-year."
include_graphics(here("figures", "yield-versus-precipitation.png"))
```

Each point represents one country-year. The graphic can reveal possible
within-country patterns and unusual observations, but it does not control for
time trends, measurement error, temperature, inputs, irrigation, or other
factors. It describes association, not causation.

## Communication figure

```{r}
#| label: fig-communication
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Selected communication figure: country maize-yield trajectories."
#| fig-alt: "Nine common-scale country panels showing that maize-yield levels and trajectories differ across selected countries from 1990 to 2022."
include_graphics(here("figures", "maize-yield-communication.png"))
```

The retained communication figure focuses on one comparison: maize-yield
levels and trajectories differ across the selected countries. National annual
observations do not show subnational variation and cannot identify the causes
of those differences.

## Review questions

1. Which distribution features remain stable under reasonable bin widths?
2. Which countries show persistent changes in yield level over time?
3. Does precipitation show the same temporal patterns as yield?
4. How would free facet scales change the interpretation of country trends?
5. Where does overplotting affect the yield-precipitation figure?
6. Which visible patterns should be quantified in Descriptive Data Analysis?
7. Which additional evidence would be needed for an explanatory claim?

## Reproducibility statement

The figures were generated through a version-controlled script from the
prepared and integrated project artifacts. Package versions are recorded in
`renv.lock`; output paths and dimensions are explicit; and
`metadata/artifacts.csv` records input and output checksums before and after
the visualization operation.
